title: fix(ui): retire suggestions when prediction eligibility changes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A prediction can remain visible when its reactive eligibility changes without a general composer props refresh. The effect tracked the outer predictions object, then read its current fields only in the untracked apply phase.

## User Impact

Changing prediction eligibility now retires the suggestion and event subscription immediately. Acceptance, cancellation, visibility, and late-result checks still use current owner facts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare the complete prediction source in the effect's tracked compute phase and pass it to the existing `sync(next)` operation. Native event callbacks still read live input at the point of use. No new owner, cache, option, import, or lazy boundary is introduced.

This completes the prediction-input finding from the survivor audit in #178593. The effect remains because it synchronizes real dictation, catalog, and prediction resources; menu resets also retire real resources and are not replaced by speculative rendering state.

## Evidence

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New reactive-eligibility regression on original production files | Fails: suggestion remains visible after eligibility changes |
| `chat-composer-prediction.test.tsx --maxWorkers=1` | 17 passed; 2.73 s Vitest, 5.22 s wrapper |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` | Passed |
| Independent P0–P2 review | No actionable findings |
| Effect / untrack / raw listener / query counts | Unchanged |

Production LOC **349 → 351 (+2)**; test LOC **177 → 194 (+17)**. The new test exercises the actual composer and a reactive field update without a props refresh. One initial fixture attempt failed because the whole composer was incorrectly mounted under a primitive owner; the fixture was corrected and the complete focused file passed. Existing unrelated strict-read warnings remain in adjacent question/menu code.

No visual structure/style or startup import graph changes; no local build/E2E suite under the campaign budget. `ci:full` supplies the broad Chat, retention, and browser proof. No leases used.
